question: In which year did India sign an agreement with International Seabed Authority for exploratory mining?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2002.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 2002, India signed a contract with ISA and after a complete resource analysis of the seabed 50% was surrendered and the country retained an area of 75,000 sq km.**
 
• According to a release from the** Ministry of Earth Science,** the estimated polymetallic nodule resources potential in this area is 380 million tonnes (MT), containing 4.7 MT of nickel, 4.29 MT of copper, 0.55 MT of cobalt, and 92.59 MT of manganese.
 
• Further studies have helped narrow the mining area to 18,000 sq km which will be the **'First Generation Mine-site'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Seabed Authority (ISA):**

 
 
• It is an autonomous international organization established under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, allowing the 'area' for deep-sea mining.
 
• India was the first country to receive the status of a 'Pioneer Investor' in 1987 and was given an area of about 1.5 lakh sq km in the central Indian Ocean Basic (CIOB) for nodule exploration.
